ModelVariations.Name: Vega configuration families
ModelVariations.Description: Willard used the same hull families for distinct Nomad, Voyager, Horizon, Searcher and other configurations. “Vega” identifies a hull family rather than one universal layout.

ModelCharacter: The roomiest powerboat version of Willard's famous Vega 30 displacement hull: a compact raised-pilothouse cruiser with a full-width salon, single Perkins diesel, ballasted keel and genuine passagemaker-style fuel economy at about six knots.
DesignLineage: The Hale Field-designed Vega 30 family was produced from 1972–1975, with 110 hulls across Searcher, Voyager, Nomad and Horizon configurations.
The Voyager was the raised-pilothouse version and the owners registry records 29 examples.

The Voyager shares the same full-displacement, ballasted Vega 30 hull with the other power variants, but its full-width salon and raised pilothouse make it a genuine configuration distinction rather than a duplicate.
The later Willard 30/4 Mark IV was derived primarily from the Vega 30 Nomad, not from the Voyager.
OwnershipCharacter: Extremely simple and economical by modern standards: one low-powered diesel, shaft drive, large tanks and few hotel systems. The main ownership challenge is age—original black-iron fuel tanks, windows, wiring, plywood-cored/sheathed superstructure and decades of owner modifications can dominate refit cost.
